picks.what_it_does: Opus Genetics makes eye treatments, including an eye drop already sold as RYZUMVI with partner Viatris, and is asking the FDA to approve it for age-related blurry near vision (presbyopia).
picks.catalyst: FDA decision on the sNDA for phentolamine 0.75% (RYZUMVI / MR-141) in presbyopia. The goal date is Saturday Oct 17, and the FDA usually acts on the Friday before (Oct 16). Placed in Week 1, not Week 2, because the stock has to be held by the Oct 16 close to capture a Friday decision. If nothing is announced by then, hold it into Mon Oct 19.
picks.catalyst_date: 2026-10-17 (Saturday PDUFA goal date; FDA action most likely Fri 2026-10-16)
picks.date_basis: Company-confirmed PDUFA goal date (sNDA acceptance press release, Feb 2026), repeated in trade press and October PDUFA calendars. The weekend rule would put it in Week 2. I moved it to Week 1 on purpose because FDA actions on Saturday goal dates usually come on the Friday, and Week 1 has no other dated candidate.
picks.why_positive: Approval would extend an already-approved drug into the large presbyopia market, backed by two pivotal Phase 3 trials (VEGA-2 and VEGA-3), with no known deficiencies and no advisory committee. A plausible move is +15% to +60% on approval (about -30% to -50% on a rejection). The stock has already fallen about 20% from its September level, which lowers the sell-the-news risk somewhat.

picks.catalyst: Phase 3 ECLIPSE 1 topline for tobevibart plus elebsiran in hepatitis delta. The company guides only to 'Q4 2026', with no week given. This is a FLOATING catalyst used to fill Week 1. It is not dated in this week.
picks.catalyst_date: Q4 2026 (no specific date; low chance it falls Oct 12-16)
picks.date_basis: Company guidance window (Q2 2026 results, Aug 5, 2026). Not week-specific, and there is some slippage risk because an earlier release pointed to Q1 2027.
picks.why_positive: Phase 2 SOLSTICE showed 88% undetectable HDV RNA at week 96, so a positive Phase 3 is more likely than not, and a win could add about +40% to +100%. Cash of more than US$1B removes dilution risk, but the readout may well land after the competition ends.

picks.what_it_does: Climb Bio is developing antibody drugs for immune-driven kidney diseases, including budoprutug for membranous nephropathy and CLYM116 for IgA nephropathy.
picks.catalyst: ASN Kidney Week 2026 (Denver, Oct 21-25). CLYM116 posters are dated Oct 22 and 23 (Week 2), and the first preliminary Phase 2 PrisMN data for budoprutug are an oral presentation. One newsletter dates the oral to Saturday Oct 24, which would mean a reaction on Mon Oct 26. Hold through Oct 26 to capture the oral.

picks.why_positive: Selection for an oral presentation suggests the first-in-patient membranous nephropathy data are presentable, and strong remission or B-cell depletion numbers could re-rate the stock by about +30% to +100%. The risk is that the stock rose from about US$11 to US$15-17 into the event, so a sell-the-news drop is possible.

picks.what_it_does: Tiziana Life Sciences is testing a nasal-spray antibody called foralumab for progressive multiple sclerosis.
picks.catalyst: Placebo-controlled Phase 2a topline for intranasal foralumab in non-active secondary progressive MS (48 patients). The company guided to 'late Q3 2026', so the data are overdue. A presentation is planned at the joint ACTRIMS-ECTRIMS meeting in Toronto, Oct 21-23.
picks.catalyst_date: 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-23 (conference); topline is overdue and could come any day
picks.date_basis: Company guidance (May 21, 2026 release) plus the conference dates from event listings. Tiziana's exact slot is not confirmed.
picks.why_positive: Earlier uncontrolled expanded-access data were encouraging (14 patients improved or stable), and a clean placebo-controlled signal in a micro-cap could move the stock +50% to +200%. Odds are low (BiopharmaWatch puts the probability of success at about 20%), and the price sits just above the US$1.00 floor, so check the live quote before buying.

picks.what_it_does: Inovio makes DNA-based medicines, and its lead drug INO-3107 treats recurrent respiratory papillomatosis, a rare disease that causes growths in the airway.
picks.catalyst: FDA PDUFA goal date for the INO-3107 BLA (accelerated approval). Oct 30 is a Friday. A decision after the close would be traded Mon Nov 2 (Week 4), so hold it over the weekend if no news has come by the close.
picks.date_basis: Company-confirmed (Q1 and Q2 2026 results; unchanged as of the Aug 12 report, with the late-cycle review and inspections complete). Also on October PDUFA calendars.
picks.why_positive: Approval of the company's only near-term asset could move a stock with a 52-week range of US$0.56-2.98 by about +80% to +200%, and one calendar puts approval odds at about 70%. The risks are serious: the FDA has questioned eligibility for accelerated approval, a rejection would likely mean -55% or worse, and the price and market cap sit right at the US$1.00 and US$100M floors. Confirm the price is above US$1 before buying.

picks.what_it_does: GSI Technology designs specialty memory chips (SRAM) and an AI processor called Gemini APU that does computing inside memory, used in edge-AI, defence and aerospace systems.
picks.catalyst: Fiscal Q2 FY2027 earnings (quarter ended Sep 30). Expected Thu Oct 29 after the close, with the reaction on Fri Oct 30.

picks.why_positive: The 52-week range of about US$1.62-18.15 shows the stock can move several-fold on AI-chip news, so any APU design win or Smart City deployment update on the call could produce a +20% to +50% move. Guidance is flat (US$5.7-6.5M revenue), so the direction is roughly a coin flip.

picks.what_it_does: Redwire builds parts for spacecraft, such as solar arrays and structures, and supplies in-space manufacturing and defence space systems.

general_notes: Confirming the user's question: yes, the plan is 5 different stocks each week, 25 distinct tickers in total, with no ticker repeated across weeks. This selection returns only 16 distinct tickers, because only 16 candidates survived verification. Filling the other 9 slots would have meant using rejected names or inventing tickers, so I did neither. Weeks 1, 2 and 3 each have 3 empty slots, and another search round focused on Oct 12-30 catalysts is needed before Monday.

IRD was placed in Week 1, not Week 2 as the weekend rule would place it. Its PDUFA goal date is Saturday Oct 17, and FDA actions on weekend goal dates usually come on the Friday. Buy by the Fri Oct 16 close and hold into Mon Oct 19 if no decision has come out. The same logic applies to AGIO in Week 4 (Sunday Nov 1 goal date): buy it by the Fri Oct 30 close.

Some events straddle the week boundaries. CLYM's oral may be on Sat Oct 24 (reaction Mon Oct 26), so hold it from Week 2 into Week 3. INO's Fri Oct 30 PDUFA may come after the close (reaction Nov 2). ENVX could report on Nov 11 instead of Nov 4. With a 20% maximum per position, five holdings at 20% each fill the whole portfolio, so overlapping holds need planning.

Every price is stale (August to early October snapshots) and must be re-checked on Oct 12 before trading. These picks sit near the US$1.00 price floor and/or the ~US$100M market-cap floor: INO (about US$1.17, about US$95-133M), TLSA (about US$1.15, about US$145M) and BTBT (about US$1.72). Drop any of them that is under US$1.00 on the day.

Almost every earnings date in Weeks 3-5 (GSIT, ASPN, ENVX, RDW, BKSY, TLS, BTBT, ONDS, SPCE) is a pattern estimate, not a company announcement. Those companies usually announce their dates between mid- and late October. Re-check each one and move picks between weeks if a date shifts.
VIR and IVA have only 'Q4 2026' guidance, with no week given. They are placeholders with a low chance of reporting inside their assigned week.

Several picks miss the price or size screens and are included only because their weeks were short of options: AGIO (about US$34), BKSY (about US$27), CLYM (about US$15), RDW (about US$11.6) and ONDS (market cap about US$4.8B, above the US$3B ceiling). Swap any of them for a better-fitting name if one turns up.
